source: Geeska Afrika Online: 'Eritrea Quarantines Gash Barka Region, 22 Cholera cases found among Ethiopian refugees' (26 September 2016)
processing_notes: Source states: 'So far, 22 outbreaks of cholera disease are reported in the region for the first time inside the country' - interpreted as 22 sCh cases. Headline renders the same figure unambiguously as cases: 'Eritrea Quarantines Gash Barka Region, 22 Cholera cases found among Ethiopian refugees'; the body's phrase '22 outbreaks' is loose usage for 22 cases. CONTRADICTS the JHU baseline phantom zero for 2016 (JHU row 7, 0 cases) - this year is currently coded as a hard zero in the time series and should not be. Corroboration status: the count has a SINGLE origin (byline 'CDE', carried identically by geeskaafrika.com and madote.com), so it does not meet the two-source bar; it is under the 100-case threshold where a single source is acceptable with low weight. The outbreak itself IS independently corroborated by asmarino.com (source_index 11, 12), a diaspora outlet of the opposite political alignment, which reports the same Gash-Barka/Barentu outbreak in Sept 2016 and additional deaths, but no case count. Cases occurred among Ethiopian refugees sheltering in Gash-Barka, i.e. within Eritrean territory. Weight 0.25 reflects Level 4 sourcing and the partisan content of the originating article.

source: United Nations Consolidated Inter-Agency Appeal for Eritrea 2001 (published 9 February 2001)
processing_notes: Source confirms zero cholera transmission 2000-06-01..2000-12-31. Source states: 'As a result of the combined inter-agency interventions, no cholera or other water-borne disease epidemics were reported in the camps other than isolated outbreaks of Shigellosis.'. Evidence type: Inferred_Absence. Surveillance system status during absence: partial. SCOPE CAVEAT, which is why this is Inferred_Absence at 0.5 and not Documented_Absence: the UN statement is scoped to the IDP CAMPS, not to Eritrea as a whole. It is extended to the national level here because (a) the camps held roughly 200,000 displaced people in Debub, Gash-Barka and Northern Red Sea, the three zobas of highest cholera risk, and were the most intensively monitored population in Eritrea's history, with WHO running communicable-disease outbreak surveillance there; (b) the WER annual review 'Cholera, 2000' was downloaded and contains no Eritrea entry; (c) EM-DAT records no epidemic of any kind for Eritrea; (d) the second half of 2000 was the period of maximum international presence and scrutiny in the country. A national outbreak in that window would almost certainly have reached the camps and been reported. TL set to 2000-06-01, after the May 2000 offensive that created the caseload the appeal reviews; the appeal was published 9 Feb 2001.

source: WHO Weekly Epidemiological Record 45(46): Notifications Received from 6 to 12 November 1970
processing_notes: Source confirms zero cholera transmission 1970-11-06..1971-06-03. Source states: 'CHOLERA - CHOLERA, Africa - Afrique: ETHIOPIA - ETHIOPIE 6-10.XI, Provinces: Harar 270 22; Shoa 433 44; Wollo 147 6'. Evidence type: Inferred_Absence. Surveillance system status during absence: partial. Supersedes an earlier, weaker version of this row that started at 1970-12-23. Eritrea was an Ethiopian province until 1991, so its cholera notifications reached WHO under Ethiopia. Ethiopia's FIRST cholera notification of the seventh-pandemic wave covered 6-10 Nov 1970 and named exactly three provinces - Harar 270 cases/22 deaths, Shoa 433/44, Wollo 147/6. Those sum to 850 cases, which is precisely the Ethiopian annual total in the WER review CHOLERA IN 1970, so the whole of Ethiopia's 1970 cholera caseload is accounted for by three non-Eritrean provinces. Eritrea is absent from the cholera list here and in every subsequent verified snapshot: infected areas 23 Dec 1970 = Harar, Shoa, Wollo only (source_index 1); 18 Feb 1971 = Ethiopia off the cholera list entirely, Africa list is Cameroon, Djibouti, Nigeria (source_index 3); 3 June 1971 = Africa list is Kenya, Mali, Nigeria (source_index 2). Meanwhile the SAME issues carry Eritrea province returns for smallpox, louse-borne typhus and relapsing fever, and Asmara for smallpox, so the Eritrean notification channel was live and transmitting. CAVEATS driving 0.6 rather than a Level 1 weight: the Eritrean war of independence was active and rural case ascertainment was weak; and states of that era had a standing incentive to avoid declaring Red Sea ports cholera-infected because of the maritime quarantine consequences for Massawa and Assab. This is inference from an official positive enumeration that excludes Eritrea, not an explicit zero return.

source: WHO AFRO Integrated Disease Surveillance Quarterly Bulletin, Q2 2015 (vol 1, issue 1)
processing_notes: Source confirms zero cholera transmission 2015-04-01..2015-06-30. Source states: 'There were eight countries that reported at least one cholera case in the second quarter of 2015 (Burundi, Cameroon, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Ghana, Malawi, Nigeria, Togo and the United Republic of Tanzania), and 18 countries that reported zero cases (Angola, Benin, Botswana, Burkina Faso, Chad, Comoros, Eritrea, Ethiopia, Gabon, Liberia, Madagascar, Mali, Mauritania, Niger, Sao Tome and Principe, Sierra Leone, Swaziland and Zimbabwe).'. Evidence type: Documented_Absence. Surveillance system status during absence: operational. This is a TRUE documented zero, not an inferred one. The same paragraph separately names 21 Member States that 'did not report during the second quarter of 2015' - Eritrea is NOT in that list, it is in the zero-reporting list, so WHO AFRO received an active nil return from Eritrea. The bulletin states the rule explicitly: 'The IDSR requires that all Member States report to WHO and reporting a zero case is equally as important as reporting a case.' Surveillance corroboration: the WHO Eritrea IDSR quarterly bulletin for Q1 2015 (source_index 7) records 264 reporting health facilities across the six zobas at 98.3% timeliness and 98.7% completeness, with cholera weekly-notifiable under mandatory zero reporting. Q2 2015 is not one of the four listed effective gaps - JHU carries a phantom zero for 2015 - but replacing a phantom zero with an evidenced one materially improves the weekly series, and this source type is the route to closing the real gaps.
